p.src: On the evening they arrive in Xi'an, the four guides lay out what they need for the next morning. The check is short: two compare booking names with identity documents, one reads the station on the return ticket, and one opens the route notebook at the weather and hotel address. The city wall is outside the window, but nobody adds another attraction. Tomorrow depends on four pieces of evidence: the document used to book, a record that clearly shows the booking succeeded, the latest weather and opening information checked before they leave, and a Chinese address they can show offline. They check those four, then put the rest of the plans away.

caption.ja: 西安に着いた夜、四人が確かめるのは、翌朝に使う証明書、予約完了の記録、最新の天候と開館・開放情報、通信がなくても示せる中国語の住所だけである。窓の向こうに城壁が見えても、予定は増やさない。
caption.en: On the evening they arrive in Xi'an, the four guides check only what tomorrow requires: matching documents, confirmed bookings, current conditions and an offline Chinese address. The wall is outside the window; it is not a reason to add another stop.

p.src: Put the immovable items on one line first: confirmed timed bookings, a train or flight departure, and any hotel contact required by a stated time. Place at most one nearby stop before or after each fixed point, then choose the meal. Record only four fields beside every item: date and slot, Chinese place name, identity document used, and the replacement if it fails. A search result, completed prefill, payment screen or promise in a chat is not a booking confirmation. Both travelers should open the booking details once, compare name, date, place and status, then keep a version that either person can retrieve offline.

p.src: The Shaanxi History Museum main site currently says reservations for the basic exhibition open five days ahead at 17:00. Visitors may prefill the date, slot and visitor details, but completing the prefill does not secure a place. Check that the result appears on the site's Successful Orders page. Non-mainland visitors may use listed documents including passports and must bring the original document used to book together with the confirmation. The Emperor Qinshihuang's Mausoleum Site Museum currently uses real-name reservation through its official website or official WeChat channels, accepts passport details, checks the original valid document at entry, and requires a reservation even for free-entry categories. These rules can change. Near departure, return to ticketing through the venue's own site, not an old QR code, search advertisement or resale link.

p.src: If the Shaanxi History Museum booking fails, do not keep the original route and squeeze another museum into it. Replace the whole morning with the Small Wild Goose Pagoda, Jianfu Temple precinct and Xi'an Museum, or one indoor anchor whose opening you have confirmed; keep the afternoon in the south. If the Qin booking fails, remove the Lintong day and choose one complete city thread. Do not travel there hoping to find an unofficial ticket. For a reservation you will not use, read the cancellation rule on the official booking page and cancel it in time. The Shaanxi History Museum currently warns that an uncancelled no-show can restrict later bookings; confirm the period and procedure on the current page. The replacement is not second-rate if it still forms a sensible day in one part of the city.

p.src: Do not write 'museums close on Monday' at the top of the itinerary and apply it across the city. Closing days, public-holiday openings, last entry and exhibition changes differ by venue. First check the State Council holiday arrangement for that year so you know which dates are public holidays and adjusted working days. Then read each venue's latest notice. Finally, return to your confirmed booking. The official 2026 calendar applies only to 2026, and an adjusted working day does not prove that a museum follows ordinary weekday operations. A venue extending hours or changing ticket release during a holiday does not make nearby transport, meals or the return journey less crowded.

p.src: Three days before departure, use an official service such as the China Meteorological Administration to check central Xi'an and the actual excursion destination separately. On the morning itself, check warnings, rain, temperature and wind again. The top of the wall is exposed; wet paving, strong sun or wind can change how long it is sensible to stay. Huashan and Cuihuashan do not share the city's conditions, and scenic-area opening, ropeway or trail status still comes from the operator's notice. Pack water, sun protection, rain gear, shoes with reliable tread or a warm layer for the conditions you actually find, not the month in the calendar. An official warning, site closure or a companion feeling unwell comes before the printed plan: shorten or cancel the exposed section, then choose an indoor replacement.

p.src: A city description cannot tell you what Xi'an's air will be like on the day. China National Environmental Monitoring Centre publishes city daily and hourly reports as well as national forecasts. Near departure, read the current Xi'an report rather than judging by the colour of the sky. If the reading, official advice or a traveler's health makes long outdoor exposure unsuitable, shorten a full wall circuit, unshaded square or long walk. Move indoors earlier, sit down for the meal, and return to the hotel to rest. A traveler with asthma, severe allergy or another health condition should discuss the trip with their own clinician before leaving and carry medicine under their personal plan. The reading changes the route; it does not diagnose anyone.

p.src: Before a rail departure, write Xi'an North, Xi'an Station or Xi'an East in full; 'Xi'an' is not enough. China Railway currently uses real-name checks: the traveler, ticket information and valid identity document used to buy it must agree. If the document cannot be read by an automatic gate, follow the official guidance to a staffed channel. Carry the original. A trip reminder or screenshot on the phone does not replace it. For a flight, recheck airline, terminal and current operation. Both travelers should retain the Chinese station name, train or flight number, date and route to the entrance; keep power banks easy to present at security. Allow for the station's size, luggage, the need for a staffed channel and the group's walking pace; one fixed number of minutes does not suit every journey.

p.src: Before leaving home or the previous city, save the hotel's Chinese name, full address, telephone number, entrance photograph or directions, check-in date and every guest name for offline use. If you will arrive early, arrive late at night or need luggage storage after checkout, ask the property directly and retain the answer; do not infer it from a room page. For a foreign guest staying in a hotel, the hotel files the accommodation registration required by the rules. For a stay outside a hotel, the guest or host follows National Immigration Administration guidance and completes local public-security registration within 24 hours of check-in. This is not advice to search for a vague class of 'foreigner hotel'. It is a reason to keep booking names accurate, bring usable documents and learn the local process before a non-hotel stay.

p.src: Read the rules again at the entrance. Museums may set different requirements for restricted items, bag screening, food, flash, tripods, temporary closures and visitor direction; something allowed in one venue may be prohibited in another. A barrier is not a camera position, and a long stop at a case should still leave a sightline for people behind. At the Great Mosque in Huajue Lane or another place of worship, identify the visitor area and today's notice first. Dress and move with restraint, do not cross through people at prayer, and do not bring a lens close to strangers. Ask before photographing a person or ritual. Staff, signs and the current notice always outrank this book.

p.src: For a food allergy, the card should name the exact allergen and ask whether the dish contains it; add, 'If you cannot confirm, please tell me that you cannot confirm.' Do not substitute 'light food', 'dietary restriction' or 'not spicy' for the ingredient. A card improves communication but cannot prove that a kitchen avoids shared oil, cookware, seasonings or cross-contact. If the answer is uncertain, change the dish or restaurant. A traveler with a severe allergy should discuss the trip with their clinician beforehand, keep prescribed medicine, action plan and ingredient card immediately accessible, and make sure the companion knows where they are and how the plan works. Keep emergency medicine with you, not in the hotel or checked baggage.

p.src: Police emergency is 110, fire and rescue 119, and medical emergency 120. Once connected, give the location before the full story: 'I am at ____, near the ____ gate, platform or exit. I need police, fire or an ambulance. My callback number is ____.' Keep the Chinese hotel, scenic-area or station name and nearest entrance in an offline note. Even when the phone can share a position, confirm it in words because one site may have several gates. Before two people leave, agree that one handles the call and location while the other protects identity documents, medicine and immediate safety. General questions, complaints and route help do not use emergency numbers. When danger is immediate, call first.

p.src: One: the page shows a completed booking. Two: the name matches the original identity document. Three: current notices, weather warnings and air quality are checked. Four: the full station or terminal name is recorded. Five: the Chinese hotel address, entrance and telephone are available offline. Six: there is time for the return and rest. Seven: medicine, the allergy card and emergency numbers are within reach. Both travelers must find all seven before closing the bag. Fix what is missing: change the booking, shorten the outdoor section or adjust departure. Do not add an attraction. What stays after Xi'an is not a count of place names, but the wall, the pits, a pagoda precinct, the lanes and one properly tasted meal joined into one journey.
